name: LP-XDS110ET debug probe (LaunchPad development kit)
sources: LP-XDS110ET quick start guide SPRUJ01 (2022; EnergyTrace range and rate, connectors, TGT VDD jumper), CC35xxE LaunchPad user guide SWRU629C rev C, April 2026 (Figure 2-25: the probe drawn as MCU101 Rev B, TGT VDD jumper positions EXT and XDS), XDS110 firmware file in CCStudio 21.0.1 (firmware_3.0.0.43.bin); all read 2026-10-07

columns.head: The probe: XDS110 with EnergyTrace
items: Debug probe: XDS110
Flashes and debugs the LP-EM board over SWD (serial wire debug, two wires)
Serial port: one
A second USB serial channel carries the board's text output to the Mac
Power: 3.3 V out
Feeds the LP-EM board through the 20-pin edge when TGT VDD is on XDS
EnergyTrace: 700 nA to 400 mA
Measures that supply's current, 256,000 samples a second per TI

columns.head: Connectors and switches
items: 20-pin LP-EM edge
Where the LP-EM radio board plugs in: debug, serial and power
TGT VDD jumper
XDS: the probe powers the board (EnergyTrace works). EXT: the board powers itself
10-pin debug connector
Arm 10-pin cable to a custom board (cable not in the box)
USB-C and reset switch
USB-C to the Mac, cable in the box. Reset restarts the board

columns.head: What it has, and lacks
items: In the box
The probe, a USB-A to USB-C cable, a quick start card
Not in it
No target chip, nothing to flash on its own: it waits for an LP-EM board
Watch out
EnergyTrace only sees what the probe supplies; on EXT it measures nothing
On a Mac
TI's IDE turns EnergyTrace off on macOS; our script reads it without the IDE
